title: First Protestant reason: every sin defiles; nothing defiled enters heaven apart from mercy
source_text: LXIV. Rationes autem praecipuae quibus nituntur hae sunt. Et primo quidem omnia peccata ex se & sua natura mortalia esse probant, ex eo quod peccata etiam levissima, seclusa Dei misericordia & gratiosa condonatione, peccantem regno coe-lesti in perpetuum excludunt, ac proinde poenae aeternae mancipant. Quod enim peccato competit seclusa Dei misericordia, illi proculdubio natura sua & per se com-petit. Jam vero peccatum omne, quantumlibet leve videatur, in perpetuum regno coelesti excludere, seclusa Dei misericordia, inde manifestum est, quod peccatum quodlibet etiam levissimum, peccantem maculat atque coinquinat. Nihil autem coinquinatum ingreditur in regnum coelorum. Adeoque etiam ille qui vel levissime peccavit regnum coelorum intrare non potest, nisi prius Deus illum misericorditer emundet, & peccatum ei gratiose condonet.
pass_a_gloss: But the chief reasons on which they rely are these. And first indeed they prove that all sins are of themselves and by their nature mortal from this: that even the lightest sins, God’s mercy and gracious pardon being shut out, forever exclude the sinner from the heavenly kingdom and therefore consign him to eternal punishment. For what belongs to sin with God’s mercy shut out without doubt belongs to it by its nature and of itself. But that every sin, however light it seem, forever excludes from the heavenly kingdom with God’s mercy shut out is thence manifest: that any sin even the lightest stains and defiles the sinner. But nothing defiled enters into the kingdom of heaven. And so even he who has sinned ever so lightly cannot enter the kingdom of heaven unless God first mercifully cleanse him and graciously pardon the sin to him.
pass_b_english: First proof: shut out mercy, and even the lightest fault forever bars heaven—so by nature it is mortal.
Defilement is universal; nothing unclean enters; cleansing and pardon alone reopen the gate.

choices.english: by its nature and of itself
choices.why: Intrinsic desert argued from mercy-secluded consequence.
